Resolves #21794

Waits for `Neo.form.field.Text`'s worker-managed `.neo-focus` class and both fields' `250ms` `border-color` CSS transitions (`Text.css:62-80,450`, `Select.css:26`) to settle (`el.getAnimations().every(a => a.playState !== 'running')` and `borderTopColor !== closed.textBorder`) before reading `textFocusBorder` and `closed` in `test/playwright/e2e/rendering/NativeSelectNL.spec.mjs`, eliminating the under-load focus-border race observed on `#21791` shard `7/14`.

Evidence: L3 (real Chromium Whitebox E2E `--repeat-each=5` across all 5 themes) → L3 required (`AC-1`, `AC-2`).

Micro-review eligible: mechanical — test-only synchronization fix in one E2E spec with zero engine/CSS changes (`run_components=false`).

### `@neo-opus-grace` (APPROVED) reviewed on 2026-11-21T17:09:22Z

# PR Micro-Review

**Class:** mechanical — test-only synchronization in one e2e spec; no engine, CSS or example file changes, so the PR teaches no architectural concept.

**Verdict:** Approved

**Glance:** The claim is that the arm read the text field's focus border before the App worker's `.neo-focus` landed (`Text.css:62`), and that the select's native `:focus` blue then never matched the captured grey. That is the mechanism behind #21791's first-attempt red on `e2e-engine (7/14)`: Expected `rgb(221, 221, 221)`, Received `rgb(28, 96, 160)`. At `e5f288f82d` the baseline is polled until the text field's root carries `neo-focus`, its wrapper's border transitions have stopped, and the border differs from `closed.textBorder`. The closed-state parity check now first requires both roots to lack `neo-focus`, and the select's focus check reads only a settled border. Every wait is on the condition itself, with no sleep and no retry. I looked for a theme whose focus border equals its closed border, which would make the new poll wait forever. The five-theme loop passes in exact-head CI (29 pass), and in 20 of 20 local repeats per the author. The one first-attempt red at this head was `webdesktop/PhoneAndTouch.spec.mjs:109`, a known close-click flake on another surface (defect-note 29bc4f96), and its re-run passed. Nothing outside the named arm changes.

**Findings:** None.
